profile.reading: This facility in New York is attributed to Clarkson University, a private research university. A Wikipedia fetch for Clarkson University described several student facing computing spaces, including the largely student run Applied CS Labs (Clarkson Open Source Institute, Internet Teaching Lab, and Virtual Reality Lab), which also hosts an open source software mirror serving downloads for projects like Blender and Ubuntu, plus Clarkson Ignite makerspaces, but none of these describe enterprise level data center or IT infrastructure. This is very likely a university owned enterprise data center for administrative and research computing rather than a commercial facility, though its specific building identity was not confirmed.

reading: Clarkson University, a private university in Potsdam, New York, operates a colocation data center branded colo@OldMain on Main Street in Potsdam, offering enterprise-grade server hosting to outside organizations rather than restricting the facility to internal academic use alone. The service provides flexible space in individual rack units, half-height cabinets, or full-height cabinets, and offers authorized customers 24 hour unescorted access, positioning it as a genuine commercial colocation offering rather than purely a research computing facility. Separately, Clarkson researchers have received National Science Foundation grants for high performance computing cluster projects, indicating the university also runs internal HPC infrastructure for its own research programs alongside the customer-facing colo@OldMain service. The operator's own materials did not publish an exact founding or launch year for colo@OldMain, nor megawatt capacity figures, as of the research date. Clarkson's model, a university operating a small commercial colocation facility open to outside tenants in a rural North Country New York market, is distinct from the larger public research computing programs recorded elsewhere in this registry, such as the University of Florida's HiPerGator, which serves internal research users rather than paying external colocation customers.
